comment: The Uganda example labels the components as HMIS and CDSE even though it describes national electronic IDSR. It therefore misses PHSP/eIDSR and the broader DHIS2 platform pathway: extending an existing national HMIS installed base with surveillance workflows, local requirements work, training, phased scale-up and HISP Uganda support. The peer-reviewed study documents expansion to 100 of 146 districts and shows that institutional and capacity arrangements—not only software—enabled scale: https://doi.org/10.2196/59783

It therefore misses PHSP/eIDSR and the broader DHIS2 platform pathway: extending an existing national HMIS installed base with surveillance workflows, local requirements work, training, phased scale-up and HISP Uganda support. The peer-reviewed study documents expansion to 100 of 146 districts and shows that institutional and capacity arrangements—not only software—enabled scale: https://doi.org/10.2196/59783
public.suggestedRevision: Correct the mapping to PHSP, CDSE, plus the shared DHIS2 platform/HMIS installed base. Cite the implementation study and describe: reuse of national platform and organisational units; participatory requirements; aggregate/case surveillance capability; phased scale; training and support; HISP Uganda’s role; information use; outcomes and limitations. Present this as a socio-technical infrastructure trajectory.
